questions.statement: Choose the correct phrasal verb: 'Please ____ the lights before you leave the classroom.'
questions.context: Practica de phrasal verbs, Quito, grado 11.

options.feedback: 'Of' alone is not a phrasal verb in this sense.
'Off of' adds an unneeded preposition here.
'Turn off' is the standard phrasal verb for switching off lights.
'Turn in' means to submit or switch to another channel.

questions.explanation:
'Turn off' significa apagar; el phrasal verb inseparable mantiene la relacion directa con el objeto.

questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Which sentence uses the phrasal verb correctly?

options.text: She looks after after her younger brother.
options.feedback: Repeating 'after' produces a grammatically incorrect sentence.

options.text: She looks her younger brother after of.
options.feedback: The adverbial particle must precede the object in this phrasal verb.

options.text: She looks after her younger brother.
options.feedback: 'Looks after' takes the object directly, without an extra preposition.

options.text: She look after her younger brother.
options.feedback: The third person singular requires 'looks', not the base form.

questions.explanation:
En 'look after', la preposicion es parte del verbo y por eso el objeto va detras sin preposicion adicional.

questions.statement: What does 'put off' mean?

options.feedback: 'Take off' is a different phrasal verb meaning to remove clothing.
'Put on' means to wear or to switch on, the opposite of 'put off'.
'Put up with' means to tolerate, not 'put off'.
'Put off a meeting' means to delay it to a later date.

questions.explanation:
'Put off' significa aplazar o posponer una accion hasta mas tarde. Conviene memorizar esta combinacion como una sola unidad.

options.feedback: 'Hand in' means to submit an assignment before the deadline.
'Hand out' means to distribute something to other people.
'Hand over' means to transfer control or possession to someone.
'Hand up' usually means to raise a hand in class.

questions.explanation:
El contexto de una fecha limite indica que la accion debeaise realizarse pronto: 'hand in' o 'finish'.

options.feedback: 'Look up' means to consult a word's meaning or spelling.

options.text: Look up of the word in the dictionary.
options.feedback: The preposition 'of' does not belong in this construction.

options.text: Look up the word on the dictionary.
options.feedback: 'In' is the correct preposition when referring to a dictionary as a source.

options.text: To give something to another person
options.feedback: That would be 'give away' or simply 'give'.
That would be 'wash up' or 'clean up'.
The opposite of 'give up' is 'take up'.

options.text: To stop trying or abandon an activity
options.feedback: 'Give up smoking' means to stop that habit.

questions.context: Phrasal verbs en contexto profesional, Cuenca.

options.feedback: 'Called on' means to visit someone briefly or to ask them to contribute.
'Called off' means cancelled or postponed by the organisers.
'Called out' means to shout or to require someone's attention urgently.
'Called in' means to telephone or to request someone's presence.

questions.statement: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: She picked up the parcel at the post office.
options.feedback: 'Picked up' with the object following is the standard arrangement.

options.text: She picked up the parcel of the post office.
options.feedback: 'At', not 'of', introduces the place where the parcel was collected.

options.text: She picked the parcel up of the post office.
options.feedback: With this separable phrasal verb the adverbial particle cannot stand between object and 'of'.

options.text: She pick up the parcel at the post office.
options.feedback: The simple past requires the -ed form 'picked'.

questions.explanation:
'Pick up' admite el objeto de forma separada, pero en este caso la colocacion entre el objeto es la natural.

That would be 'run away from'.
That would be 'refuse to take part'.

options.feedback: 'Miss the bus' means the person was unable to board it in time.
'Lose a bus' is not a standard expression in this meaning.
'Leave the bus' would mean getting off the vehicle, which is different.
'Drop a bus' is not an English phrasal verb.

The sentence is in the past simple, where 'looked' is correct.

options.text: 'Of' is not part of the phrasal verb 'look up'
options.feedback: The preposition 'of' does not belong after this phrasal verb.
The singular 'answer' agrees with 'the answer' as given.

options.feedback: The word order reverses the structure of the phrasal verb.
The particle order 'on with' cannot be rearranged freely.

options.text: Get on of with your homework.
options.feedback: No extra preposition 'of' belongs in this structure.
'Get on with' is a three-part phrasal verb plus object.

options.text: That the team rested too much

options.text: That the team finished ahead of schedule

options.feedback: The particle cannot be followed by 'of' introducing the place.

options.text: Both mean to consult a dictionary

'Find out' is about discovering, the opposite of forgetting.
No publication is mentioned in the text.

questions.statement: Which sentence is NOT correct?

options.text: She gave up the attempt to negotiate.
options.feedback: 'Gave up' plus object is the standard phrasal verb pattern.

options.text: She gave the attempt up to negotiate.
options.feedback: The particle can separate the object, though 'gave up the attempt' is more usual.

options.text: She will give up the attempt to negotiate.
options.feedback: The future form 'will give up' is perfectly valid here.

options.text: She gave of up the attempt to negotiate.
options.feedback: 'Give up' does not take the preposition 'of'; it must be 'gave up'.

'Give up' es separable: el objeto puede ir entre el verbo y la particula, pero no puede llevar la preposicion 'of'.
